claims.text: Introducing 10% graphene nanoplatelets into CoCrFeMnNi will form a graphene-reinforced grain-boundary network.
The graphene-reinforced network will enhance thermal conductivity through graphene-mediated phonon transport.
Introducing 10% graphene nanoplatelets will improve heat-transfer capability by 25% relative to current intermediate-layer performance.
Introducing 10% graphene nanoplatelets will preserve the structural integrity of CoCrFeMnNi under cyclic thermal stress.
The predicted thermal and structural benefits will hold from 500 to 1000 degrees Celsius under cyclic thermal stress.
The thermal-transport effect of graphene nanoplatelets may depend on their dispersion in the alloy.
The structural-integrity effect of graphene nanoplatelets may depend on graphene-alloy interfacial bonding.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a 25% heat-transfer improvement, but the falsification rule accepts any improvement of at least 15%; thus an outcome between 15% and 25% would contradict the quantitative prediction without falsifying it under the stated rule.
